methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median

data.narrative:
Polar Semiconductor is a Growth-stage chipmaker that has raised $700M+ in total capital, including a 2024 recapitalization led by Niobrara Capital and Prysm Capital following earlier ownership by Sanken Electric and Allegro MicroSystems. The Chips & Semiconductors sector encompasses a broad comp universe of 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Stage-progression methodology is the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using the $700M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $840M. This method reflects the company's progression through capital rounds and is internally consistent with its funding trajectory.

Peer-median analysis does not meet inclusion thresholds; while 12 same-sector comparables exist, none satisfy narrower filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier classification without reaching the required n≥3 threshold. Public-comp anchoring via the 20.5x sector P/S median (across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue data. The triangulated range is $714M–$966M, centered at $840M. Key uncertainties include revenue scale and profitability trajectory, neither of which is available in the dataset, limiting confidence in margin-based or growth-adjusted valuation tiers.
